title: Eaddagh
description: Ten short stories about clothes and what people wear: a spotted bow tie for a wedding in Peel, duffel coats photographed in the snow on the old Jurby runway, a lily-embroidered wedding dress left in a will, a café cook's white jacket, a raincoat for an old dog in Ballaugh, a singer's concert dress altered after a broken pelvis, clothes in a museum exhibition about war, a two-man centaur costume in a comic play, the first day of a dressmaking course, and a white coat in a malaria laboratory in Liverpool.

lessons.title: Yn carvat folican spohttagh
lessons.summary: Ianto Nancarrow needs a bow tie for his brother's wedding in Peel because they are in fashion again; on a Monday Morven Ogilvie shows him the shelf of bow ties in a Douglas shop and he picks a dark blue spotted one, but not the ornamental gold buttons; he cannot tie the knot and makes a double knot, so Morven writes him a note with the steps; he practises every evening, ties it right on the wedding day, and the bell rings in the old bell tower.
lessons.text:
Va braar Ianto Nancarrow goll dy phoosey er y Jesarn ayns Pheeil. Va Ianto dy hassoo ec e lhiattee 'sy cheeill, as dooyrt e vraar rish: “Ta mee laccal carvat folican ort, as cha nee carvat cadjin. T'ad ayns oash reesht.”

Cha row carvat folican rieau ec Ianto. Er Jelune, hie eh dys shapp eaddee ayns Doolish. Va'n shapp shen dooint er y Jedoonee, agh v'eh foshlit dagh Jelune. Va Morven Ogilvie gobbraghey 'sy çhapp, as hug ee lesh eh gys skelloo liauyr er y voalley. Va carvatyn folican dy chooilley ghaah er y skelloo shen: gorrym, jiarg, doo as bane.

“Ta ny carvatyn folican ayns oash nish,” dooyrt Morven. “Cha nel ny fir aegey laccal ny carvatyn liauyrey nish. Cre'n daah t'ou laccal?”

“Bee coamrey gorrym orrym,” dooyrt Ianto.

Ghow Morven carvat folican gorrym veih'n skelloo. Va'n carvat shoh spohttagh: va ponkyn beggey bane er. “Ta carvat spohttagh cur bree da coamrey dorraghey,” dooyrt ee. Ren Ianto jeeaghyn er hene 'sy scaan, as v'eh booiagh lesh y charvat spohttagh.

Va crammanyn ornaidagh er y skelloo myrgeddin, jeant jeh airh, son y lheiney. Va Ianto smooinaghtyn dy row ny crammanyn ornaidagh ro gial son fer cadjin, as cha chionnee eh ad.

Eisht va doilleeid elley ayn. Cha row y cront jeant 'sy charvat roie: she'n fer ta cur y carvat er ta kiangley yn cront hene. “Cha nod mee y cront shoh y yannoo,” dooyrt Ianto. Ren eh prowal, as ren eh cront dooble, as va'n carvat cam.

“Cha nee cront dooble t'ayn,” dooyrt Morven. “She un chront t'ayn, agh lesh daa lhoob.” Ren ee notey y screeu er peesh dy phabyr, lesh ny reddyn dy yannoo, un red lurg y jeh elley. Ghow Ianto yn notey, as hie eh dys y thie.

Ren Ianto yn cront dagh fastyr er y çhiaghtin shen, lesh y notey er y voayrd roish. Ny keayrtyn, ren eh cront dooble reesht, agh va'n notey feer ymmydagh. Er y Jesarn, ren eh yn cront dy mie er y chied phrowal, as va'n notey ayns e phoagey son shickyrys.

Lurg y phoosey, va'n clag bwoalley heose ayns claggys ard ny keeilley. Va'n claggys shen cho shenn as y valley hene. Haink y daa phersoon poost magh fo'n chlag, as va'n carvat spohttagh ayns dy chooilley yalloo.

Feyshtyn:
Cre va braar Ianto laccal er?
Va e vraar laccal carvat folican er, son dy vel ad ayns oash reesht.
Cre'n laa hie Ianto dys y çhapp?
Hie eh dys y çhapp er Jelune.
C'raad va ny carvatyn folican 'sy çhapp?
V'ad er skelloo liauyr er y voalley.
Cre'n fa nagh chionnee Ianto ny crammanyn ornaidagh?
Va ny crammanyn ornaidagh ro gial son fer cadjin, rere Ianto.
Cre ren Morven son Ianto?
Ren ee notey y screeu lesh ny reddyn dy yannoo, son y cront.
C'raad va'n clag bwoalley?
V'eh bwoalley heose ayns claggys ard ny keeilley.

lessons.title: Cooat duffyl er y roievollagh
lessons.summary: In February the photographer Senara Tregenza is asked by a small Rhumsaa firm to photograph their duffel coats on the old runway at Jurby, and the firm sends a driver, Fintan Lenihan, to carry her heavy equipment; the model refuses to come out in the snow, so Fintan wears a coat himself, says the coats are hardy, and stands among the snowflakes; darkness falls at four, and the last picture, taken in the car's lights, goes on the cover of the firm's book.
lessons.text:
She fotografee ee Senara Tregenza. T'ee goaill jallooyn son colughtyn eaddee, as t'ee cummal ayns Doolish. 'Sy Yerrey Geuree, haink lettyr huic veih colught beg ayns Rhumsaa ta jannoo cooatyn duffyl. V'ad laccal jallooyn noa jeh ny cooatyn duffyl oc, as v'ad laccal ny jallooyn y ghoaill er y roievollagh shenn ec Jurby. Cha nel lhongyn-aer çheet gys y roievollagh shen nish, as t'eh liauyr, follym as lheean.

Va greienys trome ec Senara: camerey mooar, camerey beg, sollyssyn mooarey as kishtaghyn trome. Cha nod fotografee lomarcan y greienys shen ooilley y ymmyrkey, as cha row carr eck. Er-y-fa shen, hug y colught immanagh huic: Fintan Lenihan. Va Fintan ny immanagh son y cholught rish feed blein, as va fys echey er dagh raad 'sy twoaie.

Va'n laa feer feayr. Va claddanyn sniaghtee tuittym tra ren Fintan y greienys y chur 'sy charr. Ec nuy er y chlag, haink çhellvane veih'n ven aeg va dy chur ny cooatyn urree son ny jallooyn. Dob ee çheet. “Ta'n sniaghtey ro trome,” dooyrt ee, “as ta mee goll dy ve ro feayr er y roievollagh.”

Va Senara trimshagh, agh dooyrt Fintan: “Ta cooat duffyl orrym dagh geurey. Foddee mish shassoo er y roievollagh, my t'ou laccal.” Cha dob Senara yn çhebbal shen.

Hie y fotografee as yn immanagh gys Jurby. Hug Fintan cooat duffyl gorrym-dorraghey er, as hass eh ayns mean y roievollagh. Va claddanyn sniaghtee tuittym er y cooat, as v'ad bane as aalin noi'n daah dorraghey. Va'n gheay lajer, agh cha row eh feayr: “Ta ny cooatyn shoh tramylt,” dooyrt Fintan. “Va cooat duffyl ec my ayr, as v'eh foast mie lurg queig bleeaney jeig. Cha nel y gheay goll trooid.”

Ghow Senara jallooyn rish tree ooryn. Ec kiare er y chlag, haink y dorraghys. Va'n dorraghys çheet dy tappee 'sy gheurey, as va'n roievollagh gyn soilshey. Ren Fintan sollyssyn y charr y chur er, as hass eh roish ny sollyssyn. Ghow Senara yn jalloo s'jerree 'sy dorraghys, as Fintan dorraghey noi'n soilshey bane, as ny claddanyn sniaghtee gial mygeayrt echey.

Va'n jalloo shen yn fer share jeh ooilley, rere y fotografee. Ny lurg shen, va Senara gra dy row ny cooatyn tramylt, agh dy row yn immanagh ny smoo tramylt foast. Hug y colught eh er coodagh y lioar noa oc, as ren ad Fintan y eam “yn immanagh 'sy chooat duffyl”.

Feyshtyn:
Cre va'n colught ayns Rhumsaa laccal?
V'ad laccal jallooyn noa jeh ny cooatyn duffyl oc er y roievollagh shenn ec Jurby.
Cre'n fa hug y colught immanagh da Senara?
Va greienys trome eck, as cha row carr eck.
Cre ren y ven aeg tra haink y sniaghtey?
Dob ee çheet, son va'n sniaghtey ro trome.
Cre dooyrt Fintan mychione ny cooatyn duffyl?
Dooyrt eh dy vel ad tramylt, as nagh vel y gheay goll trooid.
Cre'n traa haink y dorraghys?
Haink y dorraghys ec kiare er y chlag.

lessons.title: Yn çhymney as y coamrey poosee
lessons.summary: Ishbel Drummond's great-aunt dies at a hundred, and Ishbel comes from Scotland to Douglas, where the lawyer Emeric Penberthy reads the will: Ishbel, who studies her family's ancestry, gets an old chest and a cradle; in the chest are a wedding dress embroidered with lilies, a gold chain with a small picture, and a letter from her great-great-grandmother, a seamstress who sewed a dress for the royal visit of 1902 and made her own from the leftover cloth; the cradle was made by her husband.
lessons.text:
Hooar shenn naunt Ishbel Drummond baase 'syn arragh, as ee keead blein d'eash. Va Ishbel cummal ayns Nalbin, agh haink ee gys Doolish, son va'n çhymney ec leighder ayns shen, Emeric Penberthy.

Ren Emeric y çhymney y lhaih magh. Va'n thie as yn argid goll gys mac yn naunt, agh va reddyn er lhimmey ayns y çhymney son Ishbel: kishtey mooar fuygh, as clean shenn. “Ta barrantys aym fo'n çhymney ny reddyn shoh y chur diu,” dooyrt Emeric. “Va'n naunt eu gra dy mennick dy row shiu er ve jannoo studeyrys er shennayraght y lught-thie. Va ee credjal dy jinnagh ny reddyn shoh soilshey noa y chur er y studeyrys shen. Cha nel barrantys ec y mac eck er ny reddyn shoh: she shiu hene ta goaill ad.”

Va Ishbel er ve jannoo studeyrys er e shennayraght rish jeih bleeaney. Va fys eck er enmyn as bleeantyn, agh cha row fys eck er bea ny mraane 'sy lught-thie.

Ayns y chishtey, va coamrey poosee bane, shenn as aalin. Va blaaghyn lilee er y choamrey, jeant lesh laue. Va dagh blaa lilee er lhimmey, as va'n obbyr cronnal: cha row blaa lilee erbee gollrish fer elley. Ayns cooill y chishtey, va geuley airh, as jalloo beg ec kione y gheuley. Va lettyr shenn ayns cooill y chishtey myrgeddin.

She lettyr veih shenn-shenn-voir Ishbel v'ayn. Va ee ny ben obbree ayns Doolish ayns 1902. 'Sy vlein shen, va shilley reeraghtagh ayn: haink y ree gys Ellan Vannin. Va'n shenn-shenn-voir er jannoo coamrey son ben-ard 'sy çheshaght reeraghtagh. Lesh y vreid va er mayrn, as lesh y clowan cheddin jeh blaaghyn lilee, ren ee yn coamrey poosee eck hene.

Va bea doillee eck. Va kest ayn dagh laa son bee as son argid. Hooar y dooinney eck baase aeg, as va kest mooar eck son queig paitçhyn. Va'n kest shen ry-akin 'sy lettyr, agh va'n obbyr eck aalin foast.

Va'n clean jeant ec y dooinney eck, roish my hooar eh baase. Va'n fuygh doo as cronnal, as va lilee beg giarit er. Va dy chooilley lhiannoo 'sy lught-thie er chadley 'sy chlean shen, keead blein. Va ennym dagh lhiannoo giarit er y fuygh.

Dooyrt Emeric: “She red cronnal eh, lettyr as coamrey veih'n un ven. T'ad feeu mooarane da'n shennayraght eu.”

Ghow Ishbel yn kishtey, yn clean as y geuley lhee gys Nalbin. Nish, ta'n geuley urree dagh Jedoonee, as ta'n jalloo beg 'sy gheuley faggys da'n chree eck.

Feyshtyn:
Cre hug y naunt da Ishbel 'sy çhymney?
Hug ee kishtey mooar fuygh as clean shenn da Ishbel.
Quoi va barrantys echey fo'n çhymney?
Va barrantys ec Emeric, yn leighder, fo'n çhymney.
Cre va er y choamrey poosee?
Va blaaghyn lilee er y choamrey, jeant lesh laue.
Cre va ayns cooill y chishtey?
Va geuley airh as lettyr shenn ayns cooill y chishtey.
Cre'n shilley reeraghtagh va ayn ayns 1902?
Haink y ree gys Ellan Vannin.
Quoi ren y clean?
Ren dooinney yn shenn-shenn-voir y clean, roish my hooar eh baase.

lessons.title: Yn jaggad bane
lessons.summary: Oonagh Mulcahy runs a small café on the beach at Peel, and her son Ruairi gives her a clean white cook's jacket for her birthday; during the day it gets carrot soup, coffee from an overfull filter, mustard, mango juice from a small funnel and chocolate on it, and at four the children see dolphins off the beach; in the evening every stain washes out except the mustard, and Oonagh says that is fine.
lessons.text:
Ta thie-bee beg ec Oonagh Mulcahy er y traie ayns Pheeil. She coagyrey ee, as t'ee jannoo yn obbyr ooilley 'sy chuishlin hene. Er y laa ruggyree eck, hug y mac eck, Ruairi, jaggad noa jee: jaggad bane coagyrey, glen as gial. “Ta'n jaggad shenn ayd lane dy ghaah,” dooyrt eh. “Ta shoh glen. Cur ort eh jiu.”

Hug Oonagh y jaggad bane urree, as ghow ee toshiaght er yn obbyr.

Ec shiaght er y chlag 'sy voghrey, ren ee awree carradje. Ghiare ee ny carradjeyn, as hug ee ad ayns saagh mooar lesh ushtey as sollan. Tra va ny carradjeyn coagyrit, ren ee ad y vrishey, as va awree mie ayn. Va ponk beg oranje er y jaggad noa: awree carradje.

Ec nuy er y chlag, va'n chied sleih ayns y thie-bee. Va dooinney laccal caffee, as hug Oonagh shollane noa er y saagh caffee. Haink y caffee trooid dy moal, as va'n soar aalin. Agh va'n shollane ro lane, as haink caffee harrish y voayrd. Nish va ponk dhone er y jaggad.

Ec daa-yeig er y chlag, va feill coagyrit ayns arran, lesh mustart. Va'n mustart buigh as lajer. Haink y mustart ass y saagh dy tappee, as huitt beggan er y jaggad.

Ec daa er y chlag, ren Oonagh jough mango son ny paitçhyn. Va daa mango mooar eck, as va soolagh buigh-oranje ayn. Hug ee yn soolagh mango ayns saagh lesh tunneyder, agh va'n tunneyder beg, as haink yn soolagh mango harrish y tunneyder er y jaggad.

Ec tree er y chlag, ren ee arran millish lesh shocklaid. Va'n rusk dhone as creoi, as va'n shocklaid bog 'sy vean. Ren ad arran y ghiarey son ny paitçhyn, as va rusk dooie er dagh peesh. Agh tra ghiare Oonagh y rusk, huitt shocklaid er y jaggad. Va ny paitçhyn laccal millshanyn myrgeddin, as hug Ruairi millshan da dagh lhiannoo veih kishtey 'sy feayreyder.

Ec kiare er y chlag, va ny paitçhyn ec yn uinnag. Va doraidyn 'sy cheayn faggys da'n traie: tree doraidyn mooarey, as fer beg maroo. Ren y doraid smoo lheim ass yn ushtey. Ren Oonagh roie gys yn uinnag dy akin ad.

Ec queig er y chlag, va'n thie-bee dooint. Ren Ruairi jeeaghyn er y jaggad. Va oranje, dhone as buigh er. “Ta'n jaggad bane ayd nish gollrish lioar,” dooyrt eh. “Ta shin fakin dy chooilley red va coagyrit jiu: carradje, caffee, mustart, mango as shocklaid.”

Ren Oonagh y jaggad y ghlenney 'sy oie. Hie ny daaghyn elley ass, agh hannee'n mustart. Agh cha row ee trimshagh. “Ta mustart buigh as lajer,” dooyrt ee. “Gollrish coagyrey mie.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre hug Ruairi da Oonagh er y laa ruggyree eck?
Hug eh jaggad bane coagyrey jee.
Cre ren Oonagh ec shiaght er y chlag?
Ren ee awree carradje.
Cre'n fa haink caffee harrish y voayrd?
Va'n shollane ro lane.
C'raad va ny millshanyn?
V'ad ayns kishtey 'sy feayreyder.
Cre honnick ny paitçhyn ec yn uinnag?
Honnick ad doraidyn 'sy cheayn faggys da'n traie.
Cre'n daah nagh jagh ass y jaggad?
Cha jagh y mustart buigh ass.

lessons.title: Cooat fliaghee son Pip
lessons.summary: Bethia Farquhar's old dog Pip gets a runny nose after a week of rain in Ballaugh, and the vet says to keep him warm and dry; Bethia buys him a red raincoat with sticky fastenings, hangs it on a hook by the door, and gets a harness because the collar was choking him; on their walk in the glen they see a stoat, a long-eared owl with a hooked beak and glow-worms in the grass, and a week later Pip is well.
lessons.text:
Ta biggin ec Bethia Farquhar ayns Ballaugh: moddey beg shenn, as Pip yn ennym echey. Ta Pip kiare bleeaney jeig d'eash. Ta Bethia cummal ayns thie beg faggys da'n ghlion, as t'ad goll er shooyl 'sy ghlion dagh fastyr.

'Sy Vean Fouyir, va fliaghey trome ayn rish shiaght laa. Va Pip fliugh dagh fastyr, as er y trass laa, va smug er e stroin. Va'n smug çheet dy kinjagh, as cha row bree erbee ec Pip. Hug Bethia lesh eh gys thie-lheeys ny beiyn. “Ta çhingys beg er y biggin eu,” dooyrt y ven ayns shen. “Ta smug cadjin ec biggin shenn 'sy fliaghey. Freill-jee eh çheh as ass y fliaghey.”

Er-y-fa shen, ren Bethia cooat fliaghee y chionnaghey son Pip. Va'n cooat jiarg, as cha row crammanyn er. Va peeshyn lhiantagh fo'n volg echey: ta'n daa pheesh lhiantagh greimmey er y cheilley, as ta'n cooat er y voddey ayns un tullagh. Cha nel Pip goaill aggle roish ny peeshyn lhiantagh.

Ta'n cooat croghey er dooan faggys da'n dorrys. Ta daa ghooan ayn: fer son cooat Bethia, as fer son cooat Pip. Dagh fastyr, ta Bethia goaill y daa chooat veih ny dooanyn.

Va doilleeid elley ayn. Tra va Pip tayrn er y choyrd mygeayrt e vwannal, va'n choyrd plooghey eh, as cha row eh abyl ennal y hayrn dy mie. Va aggle er Bethia dy row y choyrd plooghey y biggin beg. Ren ee greie noa y chionnaghey, ta goll mygeayrt y corp as nagh vel goll mygeayrt y vwannal. Nish, cha nel nhee erbee plooghey eh.

Er y Jesarn, va'n fliaghey er scuirr, agh va'n thalloo fliugh. Hie Bethia as Pip er shooyl 'sy ghlion. Ren assag roie trooid y raad roish oc, beg as dhone, lesh dreeym liauyr. Va Pip laccal roie lurg yn assag, agh va'n greie noa lajer, as cha row eh plooghey eh. Hie yn assag stiagh ayns towl fo clagh.

Eisht, honnick Bethia hullad eairkagh ayns billey. Va cleayshyn liauyrey er y hullad eairkagh, gollrish eairkyn beggey, as gob dooanagh. Ta gob dooanagh ec dy chooilley hullad, son dy ghreimmey er y vee echey. Ren y hullad eairkagh jeeaghyn orroo, as hie eh er etlagh.

Tra haink y dorraghey, honnick ad soilshey beg glass 'sy faiyr. She lamprag v'ayn. Va lampragyn elley ayn myrgeddin, kuse jeu, gollrish rollageyn beggey er y thalloo. Hass Pip, as v'eh jeeaghyn er ny lampragyn rish tammylt.

Hie ad dys y thie. Ren Bethia y daa chooat y chroghey er ny dooanyn. Lurg shiaght laa, cha row smug erbee er stroin Pip.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa hie Bethia gys thie-lheeys ny beiyn?
Va smug er stroin Pip, as cha row bree echey.
Cre'n fa nagh vel crammanyn er y cooat?
Ta peeshyn lhiantagh fo'n volg ayns ynnyd ny crammanyn.
C'raad ta'n cooat croghey?
T'eh croghey er dooan faggys da'n dorrys.
Cre honnick ad ayns y billey?
Honnick ad hullad eairkagh lesh gob dooanagh.
Cre va ny reddyn beggey glassey 'sy faiyr?
V'ad lampragyn.

lessons.title: Arrane er stoyl
lessons.summary: In February the singer Elinor Rosewarne breaks her pelvis in a fall on the ice, and Euan Buchanan, who helps her recover, tells her the disability is not for ever: with rest and a little work every day the bone will heal, and she can sing sitting on a stool; she endures bouts of pain, learns to breathe from the diaphragm, and alters her long blue dress; she sings at the concert in March, and an old man with poor hearing says he heard every word.
lessons.text:
She arraneyder ee Elinor Rosewarne, as t'ee goaill arraneyn ayns sheshaght kiaullee ayns Doolish. 'Sy Yerrey Geuree, huitt ee er rio er y raad, as vrish ee craue pelvagh. Va'n pian feer vooar, as v'ee ayns thie-lheeys rish kiare laa.

Va cuirrey mooar dy ve ec y çheshaght kiaullee 'sy Vart, as va coamrey noa ec Elinor son y chuirrey: coamrey liauyr, gorrym as keyl, gollrish ushtey. Agh nish, cha row ee abyl shassoo son tammylt liauyr. “Cha nod mee goaill arrane 'sy chuirrey,” dooyrt ee rish Euan Buchanan, y fer va gobbraghey marish dy chur bree reesht ayns y chorp eck lurg y craue pelvagh.

“Ta'n anlheiltys ayd son tammylt, cha nel eh dy bragh,” dooyrt Euan. “T'ou laccal aash nish. Lesh aash as obbyr veg dagh laa, nee'n craue slanee. Agh foddee oo goaill arrane ny hoie er stoyl. Ta ram arraneyderyn jannoo shen.”

Va Elinor fuillaghtyn pian dagh laa. Ny keayrtyn, haink teaym dy phian urree 'sy voghrey, as cha row ee abyl gleashagh rish oor. Va'n teaym shen doillee dy fuillaghtyn, agh dooyrt Euan dy row ee fuillaghtyn eh dy mie.

Ren Euan ynsaghey ee dy hayrn ennal veih'n skairt. “Ta'n skairt fo ny asnaghyn,” dooyrt eh. “Tra t'ou tayrn ennal dy dowin, ta'n skairt goll sheese, as ta'n bolg goll magh. Cha nel oo laccal shassoo son shen. Ta'n skairt obbraghey ayns arraneyder ny hoie myr ayns arraneyder ny hassoo.”

Ren Elinor prowal dagh laa, ny hoie er stoyl. Ren ee tastal dy row y callin eck slanee dy moal, as dy row y teaym dy phian çheet ny sloo keayrtyn. Ec y toshiaght, va'n callin eck creoi as feayr; ny s'anmey, v'eh ny s'bog. “Ta'n callin goaill traa,” dooyrt Euan. “Ta aash çheet roish slanee.”

Va doilleeid elley ayn: y coamrey liauyr, keyl. Cha row ee abyl cur y coamrey urree ny hoie. Ren ee y coamrey y yannoo ny s'lhean fo'n vean, as hug ee daa phoagey ayn son lheeys as ushtey. Nish, va'n coamrey aashagh, as v'eh foast aalin.

'Sy Vart, ghow Elinor arrane 'sy chuirrey, ny hoie er stoyl ayns mean ny sheshaght. Ta eaishtaght vie ec Elinor, as v'ee clashtyn dagh coraa mygeayrt jee. Lurg y chuirrey, dooyrt dooinney shenn r'ee: “Ta eaishtaght voght aym, agh va'n coraa ayd lajer as glen. Ren mee clashtyn dagh fockle.”

Laa elley, dooyrt Euan dy row yn eaishtaght eck as y skairt eck ny greieyn s'mie v'eck. Ayns yn Averil, v'ee shassoo reesht.

Feyshtyn:
Cre haghyr da Elinor 'sy Yerrey Geuree?
Huitt ee er rio, as vrish ee craue pelvagh.
Cre dooyrt Euan mychione yn anlheiltys eck?
Dooyrt eh dy vel yn anlheiltys son tammylt, as nagh vel eh dy bragh.
Cre ta'n skairt jannoo tra t'ou tayrn ennal dy dowin?
Ta'n skairt goll sheese, as ta'n bolg goll magh.
Cre ren Elinor lesh y coamrey liauyr?
Ren ee eh ny s'lhean fo'n vean, as hug ee daa phoagey ayn.
Cre dooyrt y dooinney shenn lurg y chuirrey?
Dooyrt eh dy vel eaishtaght voght echey, agh dy ren eh clashtyn dagh fockle.

lessons.title: Eaddagh 'sy taishbynys
lessons.summary: Leontine Carlyon gives a talk at the opening of a museum exhibition about clothes and war: a copy of a crusader's tunic with the name of an apostle as protector, and a grey shirt sewn by a man interned on the Isle of Man in the Second World War, when refugees from fascism, fascists and communists were held in the same camps; after the talk Matthias Brandt says his father made the shirt for him, and he agrees to speak at the next talk.
lessons.text:
She fer-reill ayns Thie Tashtee Vannin ee Leontine Carlyon. 'Sy Toshiaght Arree, va taishbynys noa 'sy thie tashtee mychione eaddagh as caggey, as ren Leontine oraid ec y toshiaght. Va mysh kiare feed dy leih ayns y halley tra ghow ee toshiaght er yn oraid.

“Cha nel eaddagh caggoil dy kinjagh yn eaddagh va ec sidooryn,” dooyrt ee. “Va sleih caggoil ayn rieau, as cha nee sidooryn v'ad ooilley. Ta eaddagh caggoil ry-akin ayns ny reddyn ta sleih cur orroo tra t'ad goll dys caggey, agh myrgeddin ayns ny reddyn ta sleih cur orroo tra ta'n caggey harrish.”

Va'n chied red 'sy taishbynys ny jaggad croshaidagh: jaggad liauyr bane, lesh crosh jiarg er. Cha nel y jaggad shenn: v'eh jeant 'sy vlein shoh, gollrish yn eaddagh va ec reejerey croshaidagh roish shiaght cheead blein. “Va crosh er dagh jaggad croshaidagh,” dooyrt Leontine, “as va ennym ostyl ny keayrtyn er y jaggad. Va sidooryn credjal dy row yn ostyl ny choadeyder oc 'sy chaggey. Va'n ostyl Peddyr ny choadeyder er ny smoo jeu.”

Va'n daa red elley veih'n Nah Chaggey Dowanagh. Ayns y chaggey shen, va thousaneyn dy leih ayns bondiaght ayns Mannin. Va campyn ayns Doolish as ayns buill elley, as va ny pryssoonee cummal ayns thieyn er y traie, cooyl cleigh yiarn. “Cha nee pryssoonaght cadjin v'ayn,” dooyrt Leontine. “Cha ren ad red erbee noi'n leigh. Va ram jeu er roie veih fashistaghys ayns y Ghermaan. Agh va paart elley jeu credjal ayns fashistaghys, as va paart credjal ayns cummynys. Va'n bondiaght cheddin oc ooilley.”

Va lheiney ghlass 'sy taishbynys, as ennym screeuit er ayns snaie jiarg. Va'n lheiney jeant ec dooinney ayns pryssoonaght 'sy champ. Va obbyr eiginit ayn ayns paart dy champyn: va ny pryssoonee eiginit dy obbraghey 'sy vagher. Agh ren y dooinney shoh y lheiney y yannoo 'sy traa v'echey hene, son e vac.

Lurg yn oraid, haink dooinney shenn gys Leontine. Matthias Brandt va'n ennym echey. “She my ayr ren y lheiney shen,” dooyrt eh. “V'eh ayns bondiaght ayns Doolish rish daa vlein. V'eh credjal ayns cummynys ayns e aegid, as er-y-fa shen v'eh eiginit dy roie veih'n Ghermaan. Hug eh y lheiney dou tra va mee queig bleeaney d'eash.”

Va Leontine feer ghennal. Ren ee Matthias y eam dy ghra kuse dy ockleyn 'sy chied oraid elley, as dooyrt eh dy jinnagh eh shen.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ren oraid ec toshiaght y taishbynys?
Ren Leontine Carlyon oraid ec y toshiaght.
Cre va er y jaggad croshaidagh?
Va crosh jiarg er, as ny keayrtyn ennym ostyl.
Cre'n fa va sleih ayns bondiaght ayns Mannin?
Va'n caggey ayn, as va ram jeu er roie veih fashistaghys ayns y Ghermaan.
Cre'n fa va sidooryn laccal ennym ostyl er y jaggad?
V'ad credjal dy row yn ostyl ny choadeyder oc 'sy chaggey.
C'raad va ny pryssoonee cummal ayns Doolish?
V'ad cummal ayns thieyn er y traie, cooyl cleigh yiarn.
Quoi ren y lheiney ghlass?
Ren ayr Matthias Brandt y lheiney, ayns pryssoonaght 'sy champ.
Cre'n fa va ayr Matthias eiginit dy roie veih'n Ghermaan?
V'eh credjal ayns cummynys ayns e aegid.

lessons.title: Yn kentaur ayns daa ayrn
lessons.summary: Sorcha Kitto makes the costumes for a comic play in a Douglas theatre that portrays the old gods as foolish, with one peaceful, wise centaur; Oran, the actor in the back half of the horse, calls the costume madness and is gloomy, because he has no name in the programme and cannot hear under the heavy cloth; Sorcha makes it lighter so he can hear, he learns the dance in the song's third verse, and on the first night the children shout for the legs.
lessons.text:
Ta Sorcha Kitto jannoo coamraghyn son y theater ayns Doolish. Dagh geurey, ta cloie craidoilagh ayns y theater, as ta Sorcha jannoo ny coamraghyn ooilley. Y vlein shoh, ta'n cloie craidoilagh mychione ny shenn jeeghyn. Ta'n cloie jallooaghey ny jeeghyn myr sleih ommidjagh, as ta ny jeeghyn ommidjagh shen jannoo red erbee son argid as son mooarane bee.

Ta kentaur 'sy chloie. Ta kentaur ayns ny shenn skeealyn ny ayrn dooinney as ny ayrn cabbyl: kione as corp dooinney, as corp as lurgaghyn cabbyl. Ta'n kentaur 'sy chloie shoh sheeoil: cha nel eh laccal caggey, as t'eh jannoo shee eddyr ny jeeghyn. Ta'n cloie jallooaghey eh myr yn ynrican fer lesh keeayl ayn. Ta Sorcha gra dy vel kentaur sheeoil red noa: ayns ny shenn skeealyn, va ny kentauryn joarree as caggoil.

Ta Sorcha jannoo coamrey son y kentaur. Ta daa aghteyr fo'n eaddagh: Tomos ec y toshiaght, as Oran ec yn ayrn cooylloo. “She baanrid eh,” dooyrt Oran, tra honnick eh y coamrey son y chied cheayrt. “Daa ghooinney ayns un chabbyl? Baanrid glen.”

Va Oran groamagh rish shiaght laa. Cha row eh fakin red erbee ayns y coamrey, as cha row ennym echey 'sy chlaare. “Ta Tomos goaill arrane, as ta mish ny lurgaghyn,” dooyrt eh, groamagh. Va doilleeid elley ayn: cha cheayll Oran red erbee fo'n eaddagh trome. Cha cheayll eh ny fockleyn ec ny aghteyryn elley, as cha cheayll eh y kiaull.

Ren Sorcha y coamrey y chaghlaa. Hug ee eaddagh eddrym ayns yn ayrn cooylloo, son dy jinnagh Oran clashtyn ny share. “Cluinnee oo y kiaull nish,” dooyrt ee. As va shen firrinagh: cheayll Oran y kiaull dy mie.

Ta'n kentaur goaill arrane 'sy chloie, as ta tree staayn 'syn arrane. Ec y chied staayn, ta'n kentaur gra dy vel ny jeeghyn ommidjagh. Ec y nah staayn, t'eh gra dy vel eh hene sheeoil as lesh keeayl. Ec y trass staayn, ta lurgaghyn y chabbyl jannoo daunse. Va Oran laccal y trass staayn y ynsaghey dy mie, as cha row eh groamagh arragh.

Er yn oie hoshee, va'n theater lane. Tra haink y kentaur er y laare, ren ny paitçhyn yllaghey. Tra ren y kentaur jannoo daunse 'sy trass staayn, ren ny paitçhyn yllaghey ny s'ard foast: “Ny lurgaghyn! Ny lurgaghyn!” Cheayll Oran yn yllaghey shen, as ren eh ny smoo daunse na rieau.

Lurg y chloie, dooyrt Tomos: “Cha nee baanrid v'ayn. She'n coamrey ayd ren y cloie craidoilagh shoh cho mie.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta'n cloie craidoilagh jallooaghey?
T'eh jallooaghey ny jeeghyn myr sleih ommidjagh.
Cre'n sorçh kentaur t'ayn 'sy chloie?
T'eh sheeoil: cha nel eh laccal caggey.
Cre'n fa va Oran groamagh?
Cha row eh fakin red erbee, as cha row ennym echey 'sy chlaare.
Cre ren Sorcha son dy jinnagh Oran clashtyn?
Hug ee eaddagh eddrym ayns yn ayrn cooylloo.
Cre ren ny paitçhyn ec y trass staayn?
Ren ad yllaghey: “Ny lurgaghyn!”

lessons.title: Yn chied laa 'sy cholleish
lessons.summary: Seventeen-year-old Morna Urquhart goes to register for a dressmaking course at the college in Douglas and has to spell her name; the teacher Seonaid Lamont says the course is partly academic but mostly handwork, gives each student a dress stand, marks the cloth with chalk and asks for precision in the cutting; she wears a ring-like collar and shoes soled with esparto grass from Spain; at the end of the year Morna gets work with a good employer in Rhumsaa.
lessons.text:
Ta Morna Urquhart shiaght bleeaney jeig d'eash, as t'ee laccal jannoo eaddagh. 'Syn Ouyr, hie ee gys y cholleish ayns Doolish dy claaraghey son coorse eaddee. Va ram studeyryn ayns shen, as va ooilley jeu laccal claaraghey er y laa cheddin.

Tra haink Morna gys y voayrd, dooyrt y ven va claaraghey ny studeyryn: “Cre'n ennym t'ort? Lettyree eh dou.” Ren Morna e ennym y lettyree, lettyr lurg lettyr. “Ta ennym feer chronnal ayd,” dooyrt y ven. “Ta mee er clashtyn eh, agh cha row fys aym kys eh y lettyree.” Ta Morna er lettyree yn ennym shen keead keayrt 'sy vea eck.

Va'n chied lhieen ec y coorse marish Seonaid Lamont. Dooyrt Seonaid: “Cha nel y coorse shoh schoillaragh ooilley. Bee shiu screeu ny smoo na fer ny ghaa dy screeuyn schoillaragh, mychione shennaghys eaddee as mychione oash. Agh bee ny smoo obbyr eu lesh y laue na lesh y pabyr. Ta'n obbyr schoillaragh feeu, agh ta'n obbyr laue feeu ny smoo.”

Hug ee shasstan roish dagh studeyr: shasstan ard fuygh, as cummey corp ben er. “Ta'n coamrey goll er y shasstan roish my vel eh goll er peiagh,” dooyrt Seonaid.

Eisht, ren Seonaid soilshaghey daue kys dy chowrey y vreid. Ren ee linnaghyn bane er y vreid ghorrym, as va'n daah kelkagh er ny meeryn eck. “Ta'n cowrey kelkagh shoh goll ass lesh ushtey,” dooyrt ee. “Agh ta cruinnys feme 'sy ghiarey. My vel y cruinnys ayns y ghiarey ro veg, cha jean y coamrey shassoo dy mie er y shasstan.” Ren ny studeyryn prowal. Va ny meeryn oc kelkagh, as va'n laare kelkagh myrgeddin.

Va mwannal fainagh ec coamrey Seonaid: mwannal ard, cruinn, gollrish fainey mooar mygeayrt y wannal. “Ta'n mwannal fainagh shoh ayns oash reesht,” dooyrt ee. “Agh she obbyr doillee eh. Ta cruinnys feme ayns dagh ayrn jeh.”

Va carraneyn noa er Seonaid myrgeddin, as bun jeh alfey orroo. “She faiyr eh alfey,” dooyrt ee, “ta gaase 'sy Spaainey. Ta sleih ayns shen jannoo carraneyn as coyrd jeh alfey rish thousaneyn dy vleeantyn.”

Er jerrey y vlein, hooar Morna obbyr 'sy tourey ec fer ta jannoo coamraghyn ayns Rhumsaa. She failleyder mie eh: t'eh dooie, t'eh eeck dy mie, as t'eh ynsaghey Morna dagh laa. Ren y failleyder eck jeeaghyn er y mwannal fainagh va jeant eck, as dooyrt eh dy row cruinnys vie ayn.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa hie Morna gys y cholleish?
Hie ee dy claaraghey son coorse eaddee.
Cre ren Morna tra dooyrt y ven “Lettyree eh”?
Ren ee e ennym y lettyree, lettyr lurg lettyr.
Cre'n fa ta shasstan feeu da studeyr eaddee?
Ta'n coamrey goll er y shasstan roish my vel eh goll er peiagh.
Cre jeh va bun ny carraneyn ec Seonaid jeant?
V'eh jeant jeh alfey, faiyr ta gaase 'sy Spaainey.
Cre'n sorçh failleyder t'ec Morna?
T'eh dooie, t'eh eeck dy mie, as t'eh ynsaghey ee dagh laa.

lessons.title: Yn cooat bane
lessons.summary: The young scientist Kirsteen Menzies starts work in a malaria laboratory in Liverpool, and her boss Trevithick tells her the white lab coat is her protector; she studies mosquito egg cells under a microscope in glass dishes with an absorbent pad under each, and asks many questions; a drop of alkali burns a hole in the coat but not in her skin, Trevithick puts out a small fire with an extinguisher, and Kirsteen keeps the coat with the hole as a reminder.
lessons.text:
She oaylleeagh aeg ee Kirsteen Menzies. Lurg tree bleeaney ec y colleish, hooar ee yn chied obbyr eck ayns Liverpool, ayns Sostyn, ayns thie-obbree ta jannoo studeyrys er malaarey. Ta malaarey ny çhingys trome ayns ram çheeraghyn çheh. Ta'n çhingys goll veih peiagh gys peiagh trooid y corveeyl, beishteig veg ta goaill fuill.

Er y chied laa, hooar Kirsteen cooat bane lesh e ennym er. Va'n cooat bane liauyr, as v'eh jeant jeh eaddagh lajer. Dooyrt y ven va stiurey'n thie-obbree, Trevithick, r'ee: “Ta'n cooat shoh ny choadeyder ayd. Cur ort eh dagh laa, as ny cur eh ort dys y thie.”

Va Kirsteen gobbraghey er oohagyn ny corveeyl. Ta oohag ny killag veg, as ta'n corveeyl aeg gaase veih. My vel oaylleeaght abyl lhiettal ny oohagyn, cha jig corveeyl noa, as bee ny sloo malaarey ayn. Va Kirsteen jeeaghyn er dagh oohag trooid mynreayrtan, ayns saagh beg gless.

Va ram reddyn gless 'sy thie-obbree: saagh gless er dagh boayrd, as feddanyn gless beggey. Fo dagh saagh gless, va sooder: peesh dy phabyr bog, bane, ta goaill stiagh ushtey. “Ta'n sooder goaill stiagh dagh bineen ta tuittym,” dooyrt Trevithick. “Cur sooder noa fo'n ghless dagh moghrey.”

Vrie Kirsteen ram feyshtyn er y chied laa. Vrie ee c'raad va'n stoo trome freilt, as vrie ee cre'n fa va'n sooder bane as nagh row eh gorrym. Dooyrt Trevithick dy vel y sooder bane son dy vod oo fakin dagh bineen er.

Va saagh beg ayn lesh alkalaih. Ta sleih ymmydey alkalaih son dy ghlenney gless, agh t'eh losht yn crackan as yn eaddagh. Er y nah laa, huitt bineen dy alkalaih er y cooat bane, as ren yn alkalaih towl beg ayns y chooat. Agh cha ren eh losht y crackan eck: va'n cooat ny choadeyder mie.

Er y trass laa, va aile beg 'sy thie-obbree. Va pabyr er losht faggys da soilshey. Ghow Trevithick y moogheyder veih'n voalley, as ren ee yn aile y vooghey ayns un tullagh. Lurg shen, ren ee soilshaghey da Kirsteen c'raad va dagh moogheyder 'sy thie-obbree. Va tree moogheyderyn ayn, jiarg as trome.

Nish, ta towl beg ayns cooat bane Kirsteen. Cha nel ee laccal cooat noa. “Ta'n towl ny chooinaghtyn,” dooyrt ee. “Ta mee cooinaghtyn er y laa shen dagh keayrt ta mee goll faggys da'n alkalaih.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta'n thie-obbree jannoo studeyrys er?
T'eh jannoo studeyrys er malaarey.
Cre ta oohag?
Ta oohag ny killag veg, as ta'n corveeyl aeg gaase veih.
Cre'n fa va sooder fo dagh saagh gless?
Ta'n sooder goaill stiagh dagh bineen ta tuittym.
Cre ren yn alkalaih er y cooat bane?
Ren eh towl beg ayns y chooat.
Cre ren Trevithick tra va aile beg ayn?
Ghow ee y moogheyder veih'n voalley, as ren ee yn aile y vooghey.
